vulnerability.name: Jupyter Notebook with no token or password
vulnerability.author: SecGen Pipeline
vulnerability.description: Installs a Jupyter Notebook server from the Debian package and runs it under systemd as an unprivileged service account, bound to all interfaces with an empty token and an empty password. Jupyter authenticates with a single token or password and no username, so a server started this way lets any visitor open the web UI, browse the notebook directory and spawn a Python kernel that runs code as the service user. The notebook directory is that user's home, where a flag is leaked, so an unauthenticated visitor can read it through the /api/contents endpoint or by executing code in a kernel. This is a configuration weakness rather than a software flaw, so there is no CVE. The Metasploit module auxiliary/scanner/http/jupyter_login detects that no login is required.
vulnerability.hint: A data-science notebook server is listening on the network; it never asks who you are.
vulnerability.solution: The Jupyter Notebook server runs with an empty token and password, so no login is required. Connect to it, browse the notebook directory and read the leaked flag through /api/contents or run code in a Python kernel as the service user.
